A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TyphoonMLA and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The roofline analysis and original appendix analyses can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original NPU/GPU throughput and latency measurements, and Appendix A.2 reports profiling across batch sizes.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original measurements and reports additional batch-size results. Appendix A.3 retains the empirical sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: The shared-prefix naive computation, non-shared absorb computation, output combination, and small-batch fallback are retained. Algorithm 1 and the expanded decode description document the existing procedure rather than establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU, GSM8K, SimpleQA, and the same three system prompts with DeepSeek-v3 and Kimi K2. The new end-to-end estimate reuses DeepSeek-v3/MMLU and these prompts; it changes performance evaluation rather than data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain PagedAttentionMLA and CATLASS-Absorb on NPUs, and FlashMLA and FlashInfer on GPUs. Appendix comparators are unchanged. The new end-to-end comparison reuses FlashMLA without introducing another baseline.

E3.justification: NPU benchmark batches expand from 256/512/1024 to 64/128/256/512/1024; GPU benchmarks expand from 1024 to the same five sizes. Beyond these extensions, v2 introduces an end-to-end estimation protocol for 128 GPUs with batch 128 per device, combining measured attention timings with cited profiling data for other layers and reporting total iteration time and token generation rate.

E4.justification: The new end-to-end case study tests how attention acceleration translates into whole-model gains when other layers and communication remain unchanged. Existing latency breakdowns, memory-footprint analysis, and appendix batch-size sensitivity results are retained; moving the roofline analysis does not add another analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Repeating experiments at different batch sizes does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 add smaller-batch throughput results, including batch-64 GPU cases where TyphoonMLA falls below baselines. The previously reported batch-1024 GPU results are retained. New Table 3 estimates full-model performance: for Prompt A, FlashMLA versus TyphoonMLA gives 127.2 versus 86.3 ms total iteration time and 1.01 versus 1.48 kToken/s. These extend the findings beyond the earlier kernel-only results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a derivation of the hardware-dependent break-even batch size in Equation 1, yielding B_theta = 61 for the stated DeepSeek-v3/NPU parameters, and adds CombineLSE cost expressions. The underlying computational model and relocated roofline analysis remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an end-to-end throughput claim of up to 1.48×, whereas v1 quantified attention-kernel speedups. The hybrid-method contribution and headline kernel speedups remain. Exact-identical-output wording is replaced with mathematical equivalence.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes attention acceleration from full-model gains because MoE and communication costs remain unchanged. It also explains why CombineLSE overhead becomes small at long contexts and adds the claim that prior tree-structured cache-management mechanisms can apply to TyphoonMLA.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 supplies tensor shapes, projection operations, and LSE-combination details. v2 identifies the profiling-data source used for its end-to-end estimate and changes the stated code location from acyuzuguler/TyphoonMLA-community to huawei-csl/TyphoonMLA-community; both versions already claim public code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DeepSeek profiling-data reference and refines its discussion of already-cited prefix-sharing systems, explicitly naming examples and arguing compatibility with their tree-cache mechanisms. The broader literature coverage and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 expands the decode explanation, refines terminology, edits affiliation and publication-header text, and moves Section 2.3 to Appendix A.1. Most prose and the main section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The benchmark figures are substantially redesigned around batch-size axes, including changed NPU normalization scales. Table 1 is reorganized by resource type, Algorithm 1 and Table 3 are added, the latency chart is resized and repositioned, and memory-footprint axes are consolidated. The roofline figure moves to the appendix, while the original appendix plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the existing method through pseudocode and a threshold derivation, broadens batch-size evaluation, and partly addresses v1's kernel-only performance focus with Table 3. These are useful, bounded gains: end-to-end performance remains a profile-based estimate, and broad outperformance wording does not adequately reflect the newly shown small-batch GPU slowdowns.
